Honoré de Balzac, Modeste Mignon, translated by Clara Bell.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/honore-de-balzac/modeste-mignon/clara-bell

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Honoré de Balzac, the author, died 1850 or 1851.
- Clara Bell, the translator, died 1927.

First publication of the text used: 1901 (SE colophon: 'It was translated from French in 1901 by Clara Bell.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1901, before 1931, so it is in the public domain in the United States. The edition's rights statement below says the same.
- Country of origin (not named in the facts; the translation is in English, so the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa): each has a copyright term of life plus 70 years or less. The last person to die, Clara Bell (died 1927), means the translation is public domain in each of them from 1 January 1998 at the latest. The original French work by Honoré de Balzac is also public domain in every country, because its author died in 1925 or earlier.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'Modeste Mignon was published in 1846 by Honoré de Balzac. It was translated from French in 1901 by Clara Bell.'
- Wikidata Q9711 (Honoré de Balzac), P570 = 1850-08-18 and 1851-08-19.
